guides.vulnerability_name: Windows DNS Server Remote Code Execution
guides.treatment_action:
Recommended treatment actions:  
- Implement and enforce multi-factor authentication for all remote access to SRV-01 and SRV-03  
- Apply the latest security patches to address CVE-2020-1350 and CVE-2021-31166 on affected hosts  
- Deploy endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions to monitor and detect suspicious activities on remote endpoints  
- Configure firewall rules to restrict remote access to SRV-01 and SRV-03 to only authorized IP ranges and ports
guides.evidence_name: Multi-factor authentication is enforced for all remote access to host SRV-01,...
guides.evidence_description: Multi-factor authentication is enforced for all remote access to host SRV-01, a domain controller, under control 6.7, ensuring secure access management and mitigating risks from unauthorized remote access attempts.

references.source: Microsoft Security Response Center guidance for CVE-2020-1350
Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit / Windows Security Baselines

implementation_steps.title: Confirm DNS Service Exposure
implementation_steps.description: Confirm that SRV-01 is operating the Windows DNS Server role and identify DNS listener exposure before applying the treatment for Windows DNS Server Remote Code Execution (CVE-2020-1350).
implementation_steps.expected_result: DNS service status, TCP/UDP 53 listeners, and DNS diagnostic configuration are captured for SRV-01.
implementation_steps.output_type: DNS service status / listener list / DNS diagnostics
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Save the DNS service output, port 53 listener output, and DNS diagnostics from SRV-01.

implementation_steps.title: Validate DNS Server Security Updates
implementation_steps.description: Check whether SRV-01 has the Windows security updates required to remediate Windows DNS Server Remote Code Execution (CVE-2020-1350); patch the server through the approved maintenance process if gaps remain.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Patch state for SRV-01 is known and missing DNS Server security updates are identified or installed.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture installed hotfix output and the update scan or change ticket showing DNS Server patch status.

implementation_steps.title: Apply DNS-Specific Mitigation
implementation_steps.description: If the approved treatment requires interim mitigation for Windows DNS Server Remote Code Execution, apply the DNS Server packet-size mitigation and restart DNS during the approved change window.
implementation_steps.expected_result: The DNS mitigation value is present on SRV-01 and DNS service is restarted successfully.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture the registry query result and DNS service restart output for SRV-01.

implementation_steps.title: Restrict DNS Network Access
implementation_steps.description: Restrict DNS traffic to approved resolver/client networks so SRV-01 is not broadly exposed while supporting required DNS operations.
commands: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Allow DNS from approved subnets" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 53 -Action Allow
implementation_steps.expected_result: DNS firewall rules are reviewed and restricted to the approved network path for SRV-01.
implementation_steps.output_type: Firewall rule list / firewall change record
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Export firewall rule evidence showing allowed DNS paths for SRV-01.

implementation_steps.title: Verify DNS Resolution And Logs
implementation_steps.description: Validate that DNS service still resolves expected names after remediation and review DNS events for errors.
implementation_steps.expected_result: DNS resolution works, DNS service remains running, and no new critical DNS errors are observed.
implementation_steps.output_type: DNS query output / DNS event log excerpt / service status
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture DNS query results, DNS event log excerpts, and final DNS service status for SRV-01.
